_comment: Source of truth for daily/index.html. Edit this, then run: automation/.venv/bin/python automation/daily.py. Newest day first. p = priority (1 critical path, 2 today but off it, 3 while you're in there). needs = task ids that must be done first. due = optional ISO date; a task with no `due` is due on its own day. reasons = the preset move-out reasons; `revivable` says whether a task parked for that reason can come back to the active list. A task is revivable only if EVERY one of its reasons is — one terminal reason closes it. Tick / park / push / drop state lives in PostgreSQL (v2_daily), never here, and unfinished tasks roll over automatically, so a task is NEVER duplicated in this file. task/detail/why are trusted HTML and are not escaped.

groups.title: Blocking — the journey doc feeds the master, the master feeds the .docx
groups.why: All of this is hand-work in Hiration's user interface (UI). The bot cannot create the card; it can only clone one that already exists and overwrite ten of its sections. Until a card exists under the exact name august_ic_master_resume, every export fails loudly at stage_find_master — which is intended behaviour, not a bug.

items.task: Spend time on professional-journey-original.md — his own words, his own hand
items.detail: He said this is key, and it sits upstream of everything else: the master résumé is derived from the journey document and loses when they disagree. Enriching it — roles, tools, decisions, numbers — is what makes the JD matching sharper. Do not restructure or rewrite it. When he adds detail, treat it as first-class intake: read it, reconcile it against what the master already claims, and flag contradictions rather than smoothing them over.

items.task: Open master/Abhisheik_Deo_Resume.docx in Word and check it
items.detail: The .docx is generated from the database by automation/resume_docx.py and gated by automation/verify_resume_docx.py — 35 requirements, currently 35 met, 0 failed. Three things that gate cannot see, so they are yours: the page count (no LibreOffice here, and the only pre-rewrite export was 39 bullets against today's 64) · the pale band running continuous across the tab gap between the role title and its dates · bold rendering visibly heavier, which resume-issues-to-avoid/ rule 9 records as a defect that cratered a score once and was not noticed until the PDF. Also worth a glance: the ~0.26in margins are his format and are tight enough to clip on some printers.

items.task: Close the freeze gap — a sent résumé must be unwritable
items.detail: Migration 011's trigger makes editing a sent résumé raise — but it guards resume_version_bullets, and the .docx path uses resume_documents / resume_blocks. resume_versions holds zero rows. So nothing today stops resume_db.py load --slug <a-sent-seat> overwriting a résumé that has already gone out. The rule "a sent résumé is history" is currently enforced by convention on this path where it used to be enforced by the database. 7 seats are now sent, so the exposure is real.

groups.title: Parallel — independent of the résumé build
groups.why: The card work above is all manual UI work. Sourcing is not blocked by any of it, and with nothing in the pipeline there is no backlog reason to hold off.

items.task: Source 2–3 IC seats — Principal / Staff / Architect / Solution Architect / Senior Engineer
items.detail: Never source a leadership seat and never rank an inbound one into the apply-first queue. Verify each posting against the company's own site: postings lie about location, title, and whether the seat is even open.

items.task: Paste each job description (JD) here — every one gets the full build
items.detail: That fork is closed; there is nothing to re-ask. A leadership JD that arrives still gets built too — the only open question there is whether to send it.

callouts.title: Deliberately not on this list.
callouts.body: The confirm-or-reject items — roughly 300 customers versus instances, the 70–80% consolidation, two Rocket metrics, where the +65% conversion lift attaches, the 100,000-concurrent wording, the graph neural network, the narrative guardrails, the 27 ms / P95 16 ms pairing, and the nine bullets carrying scale markers instead of digits — are standing decisions only you can settle, not day-work. They live in CLAUDE.md and none of them block today's export.

groups.title: Aezion — inbound from a recruiter, no job description yet
groups.why: Sravan K Chelimalla, talent acquisition group (TAG) manager at Aezion, Inc., emailed cold on 31 August. He named no role, no level, no location and no stack — only “an opportunity I have in mind”. There is nothing to score: a weighted rubric with no requirements to weight would be invented, not derived. So the work here is two things — reply, and find out what the seat is, on the call.

items.task: Send the reply to Sravan — reply.html, one copy button
items.detail: It answers the one thing he asked, leads with available immediately, gives one piece of evidence for each of the three things he picked out, and puts Wednesday 2 September and the phone number on the table. It deliberately asks nothing — not the role, not the job description, not the location. Every extra question is one more round trip standing between him and a phone call; all of it goes to the call instead. The forcing questions are in research.html.

items.task: When the role and the job description (JD) arrive, paste them — then it gets the full build
items.detail: Ask on the call, or take whatever Sravan sends afterwards. Ask for the posting link too if one exists — a workspace whose posting cannot be reopened cannot be re-checked. Until then the seat carries no technical score, and that is a recorded absence, not an oversight.
